setup_instructions: Get a token at browserless.io (or self-host: `docker run -p 3000:3000 -e TOKEN=my-token ghcr.io/browserless/chrome`). Authenticate with the token as the `?token=` query parameter — the query parameter name is exactly `token`. The SaaS hosts reject Authorization: Bearer (HTTP 500), so always use query auth.

operator_quirks.general: Use /chrome/function (not /chrome/content) for any page that loads rows via client-side JS. /chrome/content captures the HTML shell at load-time — late-rendered rows are absent. The page-function runs INSIDE the browserless service; page.waitForSelector and page.waitForTimeout work as documented. For pages with multiple independently-rendered sections, poll with page.reload() (up to 3 times) until all sections have rows. Always return a structured error ({ error: 'selector_missing', selector, url }) from the page-function when expected rows are absent so the workflow fails explicitly instead of sending a silent empty digest.

recipes.title: Scrape a late-rendered page and email a digest
recipes.description: Reliable scrape-then-email pattern for pages that load content via client-side JS. Uses /chrome/function with page.waitForSelector and a bounded reload-poll (up to 3 reloads) so all expected sections are present before extraction. A JS transform normalises the rows (including time-format quirks such as single-digit hour prefixes) and guards against empty results. The final step sends the digest via SendGrid. Target URL, CSS selector, and recipient are passed via workflow inputs and forwarded to the page-function through the browserless context object.
prerequisites: Browserless connector with a valid API token
SendGrid connector with a verified sender address and Mail Send permission
Target page URL and the CSS selector for the expected content rows — probe /chrome/function with a minimal page-function first to confirm the selector returns rows before saving this workflow
recipes.author: subkit-builtin

workflow.name: browserless-scrape-then-email-digest
workflow.description: Scrape a late-rendered page via /chrome/function with bounded reload-polling, normalise rows in JS, send a digest email via SendGrid.

target_url.description: Full URL of the page to scrape

row_selector.description: CSS selector matching each result row

digest_recipient.description: Email address to send the digest to

digest_subject.description: Subject line of the digest email

body.code: export default async ({ page, context }) => { const url = context.TARGET_URL; const sel = context.ROW_SELECTOR; await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); let rows = []; for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { try { await page.waitForSelector(sel, { timeout: 15000 }); } catch (_) { return { data: { error: 'selector_missing', selector: sel, url: page.url() }, type: 'application/json' }; } rows = await page.evaluate((s) => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(s)).map((r) => ({ text: r.textContent.trim() })), sel); if (rows.length > 0) break; if (i < 2) await page.reload({ waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); } if (!rows.length) return { data: { error: 'no_rows_after_retries', selector: sel, url: page.url() }, type: 'application/json' }; return { data: rows, type: 'application/json' }; }

steps.expression: const result = input.scope.scrape.data; if (result && result.error) { throw new Error('Scrape failed: ' + result.error + ' (selector: ' + result.selector + ')'); } const rawRows = Array.isArray(result) ? result : []; const fixedRows = rawRows.map((r) => { const t = (r.text || '').trim(); return { text: t.replace(/\b(\d):/g, '0$1:') }; }); if (!fixedRows.length) { throw new Error('Scrape returned 0 rows — verify the selector and retry'); } return { rows: fixedRows, count: fixedRows.length };
return { rows_found: input.scope.normalise.data.count, digest_sent: (input.scope.send_digest.status_code >= 200 && input.scope.send_digest.status_code < 300) };

recipes.description: Open a pull request, then pause until a reviewer POSTs an `pr_approved` signal to /v1/executions/{execution_id}/signals (typically via a portal-token approval link), then merge. recipes.title: Daily check: are any HubSpot deals due for a postmortem in N days?
recipes.description: Schedule + State multi-day lifecycle. Every morning the workflow scans HubSpot for closed-lost deals whose `closedate` falls within the next N days (`days` input, default 7), reads the previous run's deal snapshot (`last_postmortem_sweep`) from persistent state, flags which in-window deals are new since that sweep, and persists the current snapshot after the read succeeds. Adapt to any HubSpot lifecycle (renewal-due-in-30-days, contract-expiring, dormant-account-recheck) — the pattern is `state_read → query → branch → state_write`, never a multi-day in-flight wait.
prerequisites: HubSpot connector with read access to /crm/v3/objects/deals
recipes.author: subkit-builtin

workflow.name: hubspot-postmortem-due-via-state
workflow.description: Daily HubSpot deal sweep: surface closed-lost deals whose closedate falls within the next N days and flag the ones not seen in the previous run's snapshot.

days.description: Window size in days, counted from now.

steps.expression: const fromMs = Date.now(); const days = Number(input.input?.days ?? 7); return { from_ms: String(fromMs), until_ms: String(fromMs + days * 86400000) };

const days = Number(input.input?.days ?? 7); const fromMs = Number(input.scope.sweep_window?.from_ms ?? Date.now()); const untilMs = fromMs + days * 86400000; const prior = input.scope.$state?.last_postmortem_sweep; const priorIds = new Set((Array.isArray(prior) ? prior : []).map((d) => d.id)); const rows = Array.isArray(input.scope.deals_due) ? input.scope.deals_due : (input.scope.deals_due?.results ?? []); const due = rows.filter((d) => { const p = d.properties ?? {}; const closeMs = Date.parse(p.closedate); return p.dealstage === 'closedlost' && closeMs >= fromMs && closeMs <= untilMs; }); return { swept_at: new Date(fromMs).toISOString(), window_days: days, prior_sweep_size: Array.isArray(prior) ? prior.length : null, deals_in_window: due.length, new_since_last_sweep: due.filter((d) => !priorIds.has(d.id)).length, deals: due.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, dealname: d.properties.dealname, closedate: d.properties.closedate, seen_before: priorIds.has(d.id) })) };

Replaces the multi-day-wait anti-pattern: subkit's mental model is *trigger fires run, run terminates* — not *function that sleeps for days*. Adapt to dunning (D1/D3/D7 reminders), trial nurture (Day 1/3/7/14), and any other lifecycle whose cadence is daily-or-coarser.

name: Supabase
setup_instructions: Configure saved connector header credentials for the requirements of your Supabase deployment. Supabase gateways commonly require `apikey: <public anon key>` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; when user-scoped RLS is required, Authorization must carry the verified user's access token through a server-side mechanism bound to that caller; never pass it as workflow input. A tenant-wide connector credential cannot represent different app users, so use a protected owner-binding RPC based on immutable `$caller`. A protected RPC may additionally require `x-subkit-token`, a server-to-server credential stored only in the connector's encrypted headers. This token authenticates SubKit to the backend; it is not `$caller`, a user token, or the public `apikey`. Never use service_role for caller-scoped access because it bypasses RLS. Self-hosted deployments may differ; verify their gateway requirements rather than assuming headers from the hosting model. Override base_url with your project URL, e.g. https://<ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1 or your self-hosted endpoint.

auth_options.label: Supabase API and optional protected RPC headers
auth_options.description: Store deployment-required `apikey` and `Authorization` values as saved connector headers. A protected server-to-server RPC can also require `x-subkit-token`; keep it secret and distinct from the immutable workflow `$caller`. Use the user's verified JWT in Authorization for user RLS.

Send the `apikey` header with the anon or service_role key; most projects also require `Authorization: Bearer <key>` carrying the same key. The anon key respects Row Level Security; the service_role key bypasses it. Self-hosted: override base_url with your own host, e.g. https://supabase.example.com/graphql/v1.

recipes.title: Crawl sitemap → markdown pages
recipes.description: Fetch a site's sitemap.xml, run one fetch per <loc> entry, extract the main article of each page via Readability, and return an array of { title, url, markdown } envelopes. The caller is responsible for ingesting the output into Knowledge Sources (POST /v1/knowledge-sources with each element as inline JSON).
prerequisites: Target site exposes a sitemap.xml with <urlset><url><loc>… entries
Respect for robots.txt is on by default — set connectors.web_scraper.runtime.respect_robots = false to bypass (NOT recommended)
recipes.author: subkit-builtin

workflow.name: web-scraper-crawl-sitemap-to-markdown
workflow.description: Walk a sitemap and return per-page markdown envelopes.

steps.expression: const u = input.scope.fetch_sitemap.data.urlset.url; return (Array.isArray(u) ? u : [u]).map((x) => ({ page_url: x.loc }));
return input.scope.fetch_page.data.map((entry, index) => ({ html: entry.fetch_page.data, url: input.scope.urls.data[index].page_url }));

const markdown = input.scope.to_markdown.data; const urls = input.scope.urls.data; return input.scope.readable.data.map((entry, index) => { const page = entry.readable.data; const md = markdown[index].to_markdown.data; return { title: page.title, url: urls[index].page_url, markdown: md.markdown, bytes: md.bytes }; });

description: Xray Cloud test-management GraphQL API. Authenticates via client_id + client_secret exchanged at the Xray token endpoint (POST JSON body, response is a bare JWT string). The JWT is valid for 24 hours; the engine refreshes it automatically before expiry.

operator_quirks.auth: Xray Cloud uses a two-step auth: client_id + client_secret are exchanged at https://xray.cloud.getxray.app/api/v2/authenticate (JSON POST, response body is a bare 24-hour JWT). The engine performs this exchange automatically and refreshes the token before expiry. Credentials from Xray Data Center are NOT interchangeable with Xray Cloud.
operator_quirks.rate_limit: Xray Cloud enforces a rate limit of 300 requests per 5 minutes. Spread bulk operations with delays between batches to avoid HTTP 429 responses.
operator_quirks.schema: The GraphQL endpoint is https://xray.cloud.getxray.app/api/v2/graphql — not /graphql. Step output is the GraphQL data payload; read via $scope.<step>.data.<field>. GraphQL errors fail the step and surface on $scope.<step>.error.

name: App Store Connect
description: App Store Connect REST API for app metadata, TestFlight builds, beta groups, testers, and public links.
setup_instructions: Create an App Store Connect API key and save its private key as this connector's signed-JWT credential. Set the Key ID as key_id. For a team key, set issuer to the Issuer ID shown in App Store Connect. For an individual key, leave issuer empty and set subject to user. The template always signs ES256 JWTs for audience appstoreconnect-v1 with a five-minute lifetime; it does not use OAuth or a token endpoint.
